study_identification.title: Beyond homogeneity: charting the landscape of heterogeneity in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric electroencephalography

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantify the electrophysiological heterogeneity of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (ADHD, ASD, anxiety, and learning disorders) by combining high-density EEG with normative modeling of spectral power and functional connectivity.

hc_age.answer: mean 9.99; sd 3.06; min 5; max 18 (for the whole cohort)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Bad channel detection and interpolation using pyprep (RANSAC-based). ICA with IClabel for eye blink artifact rejection. Bad epoch rejection using Autoreject toolbox.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Site was included as a fixed effect covariate in the GAMLSS models for spectral power (theta, alpha, beta bands).

response_variable.answer: Relative spectral power; Amplitude Envelope Correlation (AEC)

predictor_effects.answer: Age was modeled using fractional polynomials. Sex and Site were modeled as fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study explicitly models nuisance variables like age, sex, and site as covariates within the GAMLSS framework. This is a direct approach to handle nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The selection of model covariates beyond age (sex, and site/study as both a /uniFB01 xed effect and a random effect) is performed empirically. Each covariate is sequentially integrated into the parameter formulas. Next, the models are compared based on their BIC scores. The model yielding the lowest BIC score is selected, determining whether the covariates are retained in the /uniFB01 nal model.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model performance was assessed using residual plots and bootstrap analysis on the training set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Residual plots: To assess the performance of our models, as recommended by Stasinopoulos et al. [55] we inspected their Q-Q plots... Bootstrap analysis: The robustness and reliability of our model were assessed using bootstrap analysis. The original training set was resampled 1000 times with replacement, with the model being retrained on each of these resampled datasets.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: A held-out test set of healthy controls was used to compare against the clinical groups. The deviation scores of this HC(test) group were analyzed and compared to the patient groups.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Models were trained on 448 (52% M) healthy controls (HC) and 112 (55% M) healthy subjects were held out as a comparison group against the clinical cohort. Subsequently, we project the test data (i.e., relative power and functional connectivity values), of our clinical groups (ADHD, ASD, ANX, LD) and the held-out healthy control group HC(test), onto the corresponding models.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Results, Data description; Methods, Deviation scores / overlap maps

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not mention validating the model on a completely different domain (e.g., a dataset from a different country or with different acquisition parameters not included in the training).
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The paper focuses on the heterogeneity within the described cohorts. There is no mention of external validation on a different domain.

diseases_studied.answer: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD); Autism spectrum disorder (ASD); Anxiety (ANX); Learning disorder (LD)

clinical_groups_age.answer: mean 9.99; sd 3.06; min 5; max 18 (for the whole cohort)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score (normalized quantile residuals); Extreme deviation defined as |z-score| > 2; Global deviation score (average z-score of extremely deviated channels/connections)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Network-based statistics (NBS) to compare deviation score matrices between groups. Spearman correlation between global deviation scores and total ADOS scores in ASD.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Deviations from normative EEG models in patients with neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders are highly heterogeneous and frequency-dependent.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study found that EEG spectral power and functional connectivity deviations in patients were highly heterogeneous, with spatial overlap not exceeding 40% for spectral and 24% for connectivity analyses. This challenges the case-control approach. Using individual deviation scores (z-scores) significantly improved group comparisons (NBS found significant differences with z-scores but not raw FC) and showed a significant, albeit low, correlation with clinical scores (e.g., ADOS in ASD, Spearman's rho ≈ 0.2, p < 0.05), highlighting the potential for patient-specific EEG biomarkers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Sample size is large for EEG but not MRI standards and is biased towards one dataset (HBN). The study is cross-sectional, limiting insights into developmental trajectories. The age range is restricted (5-18 years). Comorbidity and medication effects are potential confounds. The analysis was limited to specific EEG features (spectral power, AEC) and GAMLSS limitations prevented multi-response modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates that using deviation scores from normative models can enhance group-level comparisons and provides a framework for developing patient-specific EEG markers that correlate with clinical assessments, moving towards precision psychiatry.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper strongly advocates for moving away from traditional case-control designs in psychiatric EEG research, providing strong evidence for the high degree of individual heterogeneity. A key strength is the analysis of comorbidity, showing that heterogeneity persists even in patients with a single diagnosis. The use of GAMLSS to model age, sex, and site effects is central to the methodology.
